summary: The note describes outdoor yoga and fitness classes held in Central Park starting September 5, 2023, led by yoga instructor Kaitlyn Turner and fitness coach Marcus Johnson. Classes combine Vinyasa yoga and park-based HIIT workouts, adapt to changing seasons, and build community among participants. Participants report energy and health benefits, and research is cited suggesting green spaces lower stress hormones.
one_line: Central Park hosts outdoor yoga and fitness classes led by Kaitlyn Turner and Marcus Johnson, offering physical, mental and community benefits.
key_facts: The outdoor yoga and fitness classes in Central Park began on September 5, 2023.
Kaitlyn Turner is the yoga instructor, a certified yoga practitioner with over a decade of experience.
Marcus Johnson is the fitness coach and holds a Master's degree in Kinesiology.
Classes run every Tuesday and Thursday from 8 a.m. to 10 a.m., and Saturdays from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m.
The curriculum alternates between yoga days and fitness days.
On yoga days, Turner leads Vinyasa flows and restorative poses with a focus on breath control.
On fitness days, Johnson uses park benches for step-ups and green fields for High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) sessions.
Sandra Lee, a 35-year-old graphic designer, says the classes have transformed her mornings and left her energized.
James Peterson, aged 52, says his blood pressure has improved and he is more alert throughout the day.
Dr. Amy Grantham has published several studies indicating green spaces can lower stress hormones like cortisol.
Participants range from college students to retirees.
Instructors modify sessions as weather moves from early fall to the chill of late November, using warming sequences and natural shelter.
Turner and Johnson report that participants show increased patience and consistency in their practice.
